text: Elon Musk announced yesterday that Tesla will open a new Gigafactory in Austin, Texas by March 2025.
The European Central Bank, headquartered in Frankfurt, raised rates by 50 basis points on Thursday.
Angela Merkel received the Presidential Medal of Freedom from Barack Obama during a ceremony at the White House.
Apple Inc. reported revenues of $89.5 billion for Q3 2024, beating analyst expectations by $2.1 billion.
The Amazon River basin spans nine South American countries including Brazil, Peru, and Colombia.
Cristiano Ronaldo scored his 900th career goal for Al-Nassr in Riyadh on Saturday evening.
Stanford University researchers published findings in Nature on January 15, 2024 linking air quality to cognitive decline.
The United Nations Security Council convened an emergency session in New York City following escalating tensions between India and Pakistan.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway acquired a $6.7 billion stake in Occidental Petroleum last quarter.
The Louvre Museum in Paris attracted 8.9 million visitors in 2023, second only to the Vatican Museums.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's CEO since February 2014, announced the acquisition of Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion.
Hurricane Idalia made landfall near Keaton Beach, Florida on August 30, 2023, with winds reaching 125 mph.
The International Monetary Fund, led by Kristalina Georgieva, forecast global GDP growth of 3.1% for 2024.
SpaceX launched 60 Starlink satellites from Cape Canaveral on a Falcon 9 rocket at 11:24 PM EST.
Marie Curie, born in Warsaw in 1867, became the first woman to win a Nobel Prize in 1903 for her work on radioactivity.
Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase both reported record quarterly profits, with combined earnings exceeding $14 billion.
The Great Wall of China stretches approximately 13,000 miles from Shanhaiguan in Hebei Province to Jiayuguan in Gansu Province.
President Joe Biden signed the Inflation Reduction Act into law on August 16, 2022, committing $369 billion to climate and energy spending.
Novak Djokovic defeated Carlos Alcaraz in the Wimbledon final on July 14, 2024, claiming his 25th Grand Slam title.
Amazon Web Services reported $25.0 billion in revenue in Q1 2024, up 17% year-over-year, contributing 60% of Amazon's total operating income.
The World Health Organization declared an end to the COVID-19 public health emergency on May 5, 2023.
Mount Everest, located on the border between Nepal and Tibet, was first summited by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay on May 29, 1953.
Sam Altman, fired from OpenAI in November 2023, was reinstated as CEO just five days later following pressure from employees and investors including Microsoft.
The Federal Reserve Bank of New York reported that household debt in the United States reached $17.5 trillion in Q4 2023.
CERN's Large Hadron Collider, straddling the border between Switzerland and France, resumed operations in April 2022 after a three-year upgrade.
Oprah Winfrey donated $13 million to Morehouse College in Atlanta on April 3, 2023, the largest individual gift in the historically Black college's history.
The Tokyo Stock Exchange suspended trading for the first time in 25 years on October 1, 2020 due to a system malfunction.
BioNTech and Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine received full FDA approval on August 23, 2021, making it the first COVID vaccine to receive such authorization.
Leonardo DiCaprio and Martin Scorsese's film Killers of the Flower Moon, released in October 2023, earned $157 million at the domestic box office.
The Mississippi River, flowing 2,340 miles from Lake Itasca in Minnesota to the Gulf of Mexico, has flooded severely three times since 2019.
